anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly: Application-level SQL or transactional design that requests or touches more data, rows, or time than business logic really requires.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly: Optimizer chooses a markedly sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are reasonable, causing avoidable work or poor access paths.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly: Sessions repeatedly serialize on hot buffer-cache pages or latches, stalling while acquiring or holding low-level synchronization primitives.

When all three root causes are present, the database experiences a cascading performance failure: overly greedy SQL statements trigger large or long-running executions; the optimizer, already inclined to pick inefficient plans, may lock in full scans, wide nested loops, or non-parallel plans; the resulting surge of page reads, writes, and hotspot accesses concentrates traffic on a small set of buffer pages or index roots, driving extreme latch and buffer-busy waits. Observable phenomena include: slow-query logs filled with the same heavy statements, oscillating plan shapes for identical SQL, sharp spikes in page-latch or buffer-busy wait events, CPU spin without throughput gain, erratic application timeouts, and sudden plan flips that coincide with latency or contention spikes.

Causal chain and reinforcement: Excessive data access from poor workload logic inflates the search space the optimizer must cost; if it then selects a bad plan, row counts and I/O amplify further, funneling many concurrent sessions toward the same data blocks. The resulting hot pages increase latch hold times, elongating each physical or logical I/O and feeding misleading runtime feedback (e.g., longer observed I/O latencies) that can prompt additional plan invalidations or re-optimizations, perpetuating plan instability. Meanwhile, latch contention throttles throughput, prolongs transaction lifetimes, and keeps locks open longer, which in turn widens the concurrency window in which the same inefficient SQL keeps hammering the same pages. The mutual amplification of bloated workload logic, poor plan choice, and low-level buffer contention drives a feedback loop that severely degrades overall database responsiveness and scalability.

entry.official_definition: Terminates any session that has been idle within an open transaction for longer than the specified amount of time.
entry.trigger_condition: A session is idle, waiting for a client query, while an open transaction remains active longer than the configured threshold.
entry.workload_impact: The session is terminated; this prevents long idle transactions from holding locks or preventing vacuum cleanup.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
